subject: Reserved GPU runway & isolation — discovery recap and next steps
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Price <aaron@arcadiafin.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@arcadiafin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: dedicated capacity fit

Aaron / Priya — thanks again for taking time today. Short recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. If I misstate anything, please flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points you described
- Unpredictable inference costs and burst billing from current multi-tenant endpoints.
- Latency variability during business-hour spikes (trading hours) — spikes hit p95 beyond acceptable limits.
- Regulatory requirement for customer data isolation and strict network egress controls.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Inference currently runs on mixed EC2 + on-prem GPU nodes using a homegrown scheduler; some requests still go to CPU autoscaled services.
- Models: mixture of 7B and 13B open models (quantized), average prompt ~450 tokens, responses ~200 tokens.
- Traffic profile: regular day baseline ~3k reqs/min, peak bursts ~7–8k for short windows (2–7 minutes). You’ll send a sample trace (thank you).

Success criteria you mentioned
- Predictable reserved throughput: baseline 5k reqs/min sustained, with burst capacity to 8k for up to 10 minutes.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for 512-token end-to-end responses (network + token generation).
- Data isolation: dedicated VPC + customer-owned KMS keys, no unauthorized egress.
- Operational: cost transparency per-token and tooling to cap unexpected spend.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Reserved GPU pool sized to give the baseline throughput with autoscale/burst gates for short traffic spikes.
- Isolation via Private deployment (VPC peering) + KMS integration — we’ll include an optional on-prem proxy if needed.
- Warm-up / cache strategy: prefix caching and KV cache pre-warm during known scheduled bursts to reduce cold-start tail latency.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Arcadia: share 48h sample traffic trace + model versions (Priya) — due Tue 2026-11-10. (attachment: poa_traffic_sample.csv)
2) Redwood: produce capacity runway sketch + cost proforma for baseline + 2 burst tiers (Marissa) — deliver by Thu 2026-11-12. (attachment: capacity_proforma_v1.pdf)
3) Redwood Security: provide SOC2 evidence summary and KMS integration notes (Neha) — by Thu 2026-11-12. (attachment: SOC2-evidence.zip)
4) Schedule technical kickoff with infra + model owners — proposed slots below.

Proposed kickoff times (PST)
- Wed 2026-11-11 at 09:00 or 13:00
- Thu 2026-11-12 at 10:00

What I’ll prioritize for the capacity sketch
- Required GPU count and type for baseline + burst (cost delta for burst-on-demand vs reserved buffer).
- Expected p95 latency with caching and per-model throughput curves.
- A short PoC scope focusing on traffic replay and warm-up validation.

Thanks — appreciate the clarity on requirements. I’ll wait for the traffic sample and will circulate the proforma and kickoff invite once Marissa confirms capacity options.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: dedicated capacity fit

Thanks, Mateo — that lines up with our notes. A couple quick clarifications before you size: 

- Isolation: we need per-tenant namespaces (logical separation) inside the reserved pool so that we can enforce policies at tenant level; is that something Redwood supports on Dedicated?
- Cold-starts: how do you define warm-up windows for short spikes? During trading spikes we see repeated cold cache effects that blow up p95.

We’ll get the 48h trace to you today. Also, we need the proforma to show a run-rate for monthly reserved vs reserved+burst for a typical quarter (so finance can evaluate).

Aaron
Aaron Price
CTO, Arcadia Financial
aaron@arcadiafin.com | +1 (212) 555-0110

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: dedicated capacity fit — capacity forecast

Looping in a quick note from the ops side. Mateo — I’ll run the capacity forecasting once we have the 48h trace. My deliverable will include:
- GPU type recommendation (cost / throughput / latency trade-offs)
- Sizing for baseline + 2 burst policies (5k baseline; burst to 8k and an emergency 10k tier)
- Expected monthly reserved spend vs reserved+burst (quarterly view for finance)

Aaron — per-tenant namespaces are supported as logical isolation (we can map to namespaces + role-based policies). For cold-starts, we recommend a short warm-up window approach: pre-warm KV cache for hot prefixes and keep a small buffer of warm workers that can accept traffic for 2–5 minute spikes — will show latency impact in the sketch.

I’m available Wed 09:00 PST for the kickoff; I’ll tentatively block the slot and send a calendar invite conditional on your confirmation.

—Marissa
